question: At an 85th-percentile approach speed of 45 mph, from how far in advance should the two primary signal faces be continuously visible, and what treatment is recommended if that view is unavailable?
model_answer: Direct Answer: The MUTCD recommends that the two primary signal faces be continuously visible from at least the minimum sight distance given in Table 4D-2, measured in advance of the stop line. However, the evidence provided shows Table 4D-2 values only up to 35 mph (325 feet), so the specific distance for a 45 mph 85th-percentile speed cannot be stated from this evidence. If that continuous view is not available, the recommended treatment is to install a signal-ahead warning sign (per Section 2C.35); additionally, on 45 mph approaches, backplates are recommended on all signal faces. Guidance (recommended): - The two primary signal faces required as a minimum for each approach should be continuously visible to approaching traffic from a point at least the minimum sight distance in Table 4D-2 in advance of and measured to the stop line, unless precluded by a physical obstruction or unless another signalized location is within this range. (Note: the excerpt of Table 4D-2 lists distances only for 20–35 mph; the 45 mph value is not included in the evidence.) - If approaching traffic does not have a continuous view of at least two signal faces for at least the minimum sight distance shown in Table 4D-2, a sign (see Section 2C.35) should be installed to warn approaching traffic of the traffic control signal. - If the posted or statutory speed limit or the 85th-percentile speed on an approach is 45 mph or higher, signal backplates should be used on all of the signal faces that face the approach. - For approaches with speeds of 45 mph or higher at new or reconstructed installations, additional visibility-related measures are recommended, including locating overhead primary faces approximately over the center of each through lane, placing all primary faces on the far side of the intersection, considering supplemental signal faces for traffic behind large vehicles, and providing backplates on all signal faces. Citations: - Section 4D.06 Guidance §5 (p.670) - Section 4D.06 Guidance §6 (p.670) - Section 4D.06 Guidance §17 (p.671) - Section 4D.05 Guidance §7 (p.668) Note on sufficiency: The evidence establishes the framework (Table 4D-2 minimum sight distance) and the recommended treatment (warning sign), but the exact minimum sight distance in feet for a 45 mph 85th-percentile speed is not contained in the provided excerpt of Table 4D-2.
gold_answer: They should be continuously visible from at least 460 feet in advance of the stop line. If at least two faces are not continuously visible for that distance, a warning sign should be installed for approaching traffic.
